newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM to pay NLG 46.281 each for govt shares.
newsitem.headline: KLM to pay NLG 46.281 each for govt shares.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Monday it would pay 46.2810 guilders per share for the 17.29 million ordinary KLM shares it is buying back from the Dutch government.

"We are very satisfied with the price to be paid," spokesman Pieter Wellhuner said. "It is less than the net asset value per share, which will of course be raised due to the withdrawal of the (state-owned) shares."
Announcing the buy-back deal on December 5, KLM and the government said the share price would be subject to a ceiling of 49.33 guilders, the shares' net asset value on September 30.
The share buy-back deal will cut the government's stake in the airline to 25 pct from 38 pct.
KLM said it would pay a total of 800.2 million guilders ($458.5 million) to the government for the ordinary shares and make an additional payment of 176.3 million guilders to the state.

The additional payment represents an amount of 15 guilders per share for a reduction in the nominal value of the 11.75 million "A" preference shares held by the government as part of the buy-back agreement.

The price of the shares represented the volume-weighted average of the price of KLM shares on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange over the period 10-13 December, reduced by a discount of 2.5 percent, the Dutch state and KLM said in a statement.
Payment date is June 2, 1997, subject to approval of the deal from KLM shareholders.
Wellhuner said that no date had yet been set for an extraordinary meeting of shareholders, but that it was unlikely to take place before March.
KLM shares were unchanged at 46.90 guilders on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange at 1155 GMT, back from an earlier high of 47.40.
"This is a better price than expected for KLM," a dealer said.
